question: What is the primary purpose of maintaining strict injection safety protocols in clinical practice?

options.A: Preventing disease transmission to patients and providers
options.B: Reducing the financial cost of purchasing medications
options.C: Eliminating the need for sterile disposable gloves
options.D: Speeding up the administration of intravenous fluids

explanation: Strict injection protocols stop pathogens from moving between patients, healthcare workers, and the community. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h1)

question: A patient receives an injection with a syringe used previously on someone else. This mainly threatens which person?

options.A: The regulatory body issuing nursing licenses
options.B: The recipient of the contaminated injection
options.C: The pharmaceutical manufacturer of the drug
options.D: The hospital accountant managing drug budgets

explanation: Reusing injection equipment directly introduces blood-borne pathogens into the bloodstream of the new recipient. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h1)

question: Why is leaving a dispensing needle inside a multi-dose vial septum dangerous?

options.A: It automatically expires the remaining drug contents
options.B: It causes the liquid medication to evaporate quickly
options.C: It allows environmental pathogens to enter the vial
options.D: It increases the retail price of the medication

explanation: An open needle provides a direct pathway for airborne or contact microorganisms to contaminate the medication solution. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h2)

question: A nurse uses both hands to snap a plastic cap back onto a used injection needle. What risk does this practice create?

options.A: Rapid crystallization of the drug solution in the barrel
options.B: Accidental puncture wounds to the fingers and hands
options.C: Premature dulling of the sharp needle tip bevel
options.D: Chemical contamination of the sterile medication inside

explanation: Two-handed recapping often leads to missed caps and needle-stick injuries to the healthcare worker. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h2)

question: Which group of pathogens is most commonly transmitted through contaminated injection equipment?

options.A: Blood-borne viruses like Hepatitis B and HIV
options.B: Intestinal parasites found in contaminated water
options.C: Respiratory viruses causing common head colds
options.D: Fungal infections affecting outer skin layers

explanation: Shared syringes and needles transfer infected blood directly from one person's circulatory system to another. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h3)

question: Why does an unsafe injection carry a much higher infection risk than casual skin contact?

options.A: It exposes the infectious agent to high body temperature
options.B: It removes the need for cellular replication inside the body
options.C: It bypasses natural skin barriers to enter the bloodstream directly
options.D: It forces pathogens into the digestive tract for absorption

explanation: Parenteral routes bypass protective skin barriers, placing pathogens straight into deep tissues and blood vessels. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h3)

question: What is a long-term public health problem caused by widespread unsafe injection practices?

options.A: Sustained increases in chronic blood-borne infections
options.B: Instant eradication of local bacterial pathogens
options.C: Permanent stabilization of regional health budgets
options.D: Immediate reduction in maternal mortality statistics

explanation: Unchecked unsafe practices establish reservoirs of chronic infections like Hepatitis C within the general population. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h4)

question: How do unsafe injections in informal settings affect the broader health system?

options.A: They increase the demand for long-term chronic disease management
options.B: They eliminate the need for community health campaigns
options.C: They decrease the total number of patients seeking medical care
options.D: They improve public trust in institutional medical services

explanation: New chronic infections create a heavy, ongoing burden on clinical facilities and drug supply chains. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h4)

question: What is a common patient-related belief that drives the overuse of injections in many communities?

options.A: Syringes can be safely cleaned at home with hot water
options.B: Injectable drugs work faster and better than oral medications
options.C: Injections contain no active chemical ingredients
options.D: Oral tablets are more expensive than intravenous solutions

explanation: Many patients prefer injections because they hold a strong cultural perception that parenteral drugs possess superior healing power. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h5)

question: What economic factor causes some underfunded facilities to reuse disposable injection equipment?

options.A: Excessive government funding for hospital equipment maintenance
options.B: Severe shortages and high costs of single-use syringes
options.C: Abundant free distribution of sterile medical supplies
options.D: Low market demand for therapeutic pharmaceutical products

explanation: When facilities lack adequate supplies and funds, staff may resort to reusing disposable items to maintain operations. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h5)

question: When must a nurse perform hand hygiene in relation to patient care procedures?

options.A: Before and after every direct patient contact
options.B: Only at the beginning of the morning shift
options.C: Exclusively after removing sterile surgical gloves
options.D: Only when hands appear visibly soiled with dirt

explanation: Hand hygiene interrupts the transfer of micro-organisms between the nurse, the environment, and the patient. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h6)

question: What is the relationship between wearing medical gloves and performing hand hygiene?

options.A: Hand hygiene is only required if gloves tear during use
options.B: Gloves eliminate all microbial transmission risks completely
options.C: Washing gloved hands makes them safe for reuse
options.D: Gloves do not replace the need for proper handwashing

explanation: Microorganisms can multiply rapidly inside gloves, and hands must be washed immediately after glove removal. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h6)

question: Where should a used syringe and needle be placed immediately after administration?

options.A: In a puncture-resistant safety box near the patient
options.B: Inside a regular black polythene household waste bin
options.C: In an open basin on the general nursing workstation
options.D: On the clean medication tray for later sorting

explanation: Immediate disposal into a dedicated sharp container prevents accidental needle sticks to staff and bystanders. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h7)

question: What hazard is created when a sharp disposal box is stuffed past its recommended fill line?

options.A: Protruding needles increase the risk of puncture injuries
options.B: The container releases toxic gases into the ward air
options.C: The plastic container dissolves from chemical reactions
options.D: The stored waste automatically becomes completely sterile

explanation: Overfilled boxes expose sharp tips, endangering nurses, cleaners, and waste management personnel. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h7)

question: What is an effective way for nurses to address community myths about injections?

options.A: Banning all patients from receiving prescription drugs
options.B: Stopping the administration of all vaccines in public clinics
options.C: Punishing clients who ask questions about medical care
options.D: Conducting health education talks on safe medication use

explanation: Community health education corrects misconceptions and empowers individuals to demand safe injection practices. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h8)

question: Why is patient empowerment an important strategy for improving injection safety in clinical facilities?

options.A: It speeds up patient discharge processes significantly
options.B: It removes all legal responsibility from the nursing staff
options.C: It eliminates the need for hospital management committees
options.D: Informed patients can actively participate in demanding safe practices

explanation: When patients understand what sterile equipment looks like, they can spot and question unsafe behaviors. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h8)
